The LactMed record supports the infant-level data limitation, observed outcomes, uncertainty, revision information, and application notices.
The cited study is the telephone follow-up source reporting diarrhea and no rash or candidiasis.
The cited study is the source for two cases of diarrhea and one rash among 40 exposed infants.
The cited study supports the 8.3% reaction rate and the reported rash and somnolence.

The cited report supports mild diarrhea in the infant and the possible-or-probable relationship assessment.

judgment.rationale: The answer separates measured milk concentrations, observed infant symptoms, and monitoring advice; correctly explains that the monitoring list came from study data collection rather than a retrieved LactMed recommendation; discloses missing infant-level information and bounded-record uncertainty; and gives no dose or dosing instruction. The only minor citation issue is that the file-list citation does not independently establish the package date, and the general MCP continuity notice is not directly cited.
